AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 27.12.2021 PASSED IN MVC NO.1318/2019 ON THE FILE OF THE VII ADDITIONAL DISTRICT JUDGE, MEMBER AND MACT,
TUMAKURU, DISMISSING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION.

THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL, HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED ON 21ST SEPTEMBER 2023, COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT, THIS DAY,
UMESH M ADIGA J, DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This is claimant's appeal against judgment and award passed in M.V.C.No.1318 of 2019 dated 27.12.2021 on the file of VII Additional District Judge and MACT, Tumakuru (hereinafter for short referred to as "Tribunal").
The claimant had filed petition for claiming compensation and the said claim petition was dismissed by the impugned judgment and award.
Same is challenged in the present appeal.
2. We refer to the parties as per their rank before the Tribunal.

3. It is the case of claimants that on 22.08.2019, the claimant was riding motor cycle bearing Registration No.KA-06-ES-1151 from Nagavalli village to GH Risala village and was going on Nagavalli to Sirivara village road.

He met NC: 2023:KHC:41711-DB with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver, bearing Registration No.KA-06-AA-2068, which came from opposite direction; as result of which, he sustained grievous injuries.

4. It is further case of claimant that uncle of claimant was coming on the same road following motorcycle within a distance of 100 meters on his motorcycle and he saw the accident and shifted the injured to Nagavalli Hospital; Hearing information, father of the claimant also came to the said hospital.
Thereafter, both father and uncle of claimant took him to Government hospital at Tumakuru and as per medical advice, they were intending to shift the claimant to NIMHANS Hospital at Bengaluru.

However, on the way, the claimant started vomitting blood, therefore, they Sri Shoheb Akthar vs Aleem on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51980514/
2 again took back him to Tumakuru and admitted the claimant in Siddaganga Hospital, Tumakuru as inpatient.

5. It is further case of claimant that immediately, after the accident, no complaint was lodged against driver of the offended car and after five days from the date of alleged NC: 2023:KHC:41711-DB accident, complaint was lodged by the uncle of the claimant.
It is stated in the complaint that uncle of claimant was involved in providing treatment to the claimant, therefore, he could not lodge the complaint immediately after the accident.
It is further contention of the claimant that he had taken treatment in Siddaganga Hospital, Tumakuru and in some other Hospitals.
6. It is further case of claimant that he was working as Salesman in RF World Sales and Services Centre at Nagavalli and earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.
Claimant sustained grievous head injury in the accident and could not recover completely; as a result of injury he has been bedridden and wheelchair bound.
He had spent huge sum of money towards treatment.
With these reasons, prayed to award compensation of Rs.25 lakhs.
7. Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offended car.
Respondent No.1 did not file any response before the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 contended that the complaint was lodged after delay of five NC: 2023:KHC:41711-DB days.
It indicates that the offended car was falsely implicated in this case to claim compensation and there is no valid reason for the delay in lodging the complaint.
The claimant was minor at the time of alleged accident and he had no driving license to ride motorcycle.
He was not wearing helmet at the time of alleged accident.
The alleged accident, if any, had taken place due to grave negligence of claimant.
Hence, he cannot claim compensation from respondents.
The respondent No.2 denied all other contents of the claim petition and prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
8. From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal had framed necessary issues, for its consideration.
9. Claimant had examined PWs-1 to 4 and got marked Exs.P1 to P30 and Respondent No.2 had examined RW-1.

10. The Tribunal after hearing both the parties and an appreciating pleadings and evidence on record, held that the claimant was unable to prove that accident was taken place due to involvement of the offended car and it is falsely NC: 2023:KHC:41711-DB implicated in this case to claim compensation.
Therefore, the Tribunal answered Issue No.1 in the negative.
Since the said issue was answered in the negative, the Tribunal did not consider other issues and dismissed the claim petition by impugned judgment and award.
Same is challenged in the present appeal by the claimants.
11. The learned advocate appearing for the appellant/claimant has vehemently contended that mere delay in lodging the complaint cannot be ground to deny the compensation.
The complainant who is uncle of claimant, had taken the claimant to the hospital.

Thereafter, he tried to shift him to NIMHANS Hospital, however, he came back due to serious condition of claimant and admitted him Sri Shoheb Akthar vs Aleem on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51980514/
3 to Siddaganga Hospital, Tumakuru.

sentences.text: Under these circumstances, he could not go to the police station and file complaint; that cannot come in the way of claiming the compensation and do not create any doubt.

12. The learned advocate for claimant has further submitted that after filing of the complaint, the Investigating NC: 2023:KHC:41711-DB Officer, had conducted the investigation and filed charge- sheet against the driver of the offended car, since he was driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner.
The driver of the said car pleaded guilty before the Criminal Court.
These facts are sufficient to hold that it is a genuine accident and due to rash and negligent driving of Car by its driver, accident had taken place.

He further submits that merely claimant had no license to drive or ride the motorcycle, cannot be ground for denying compensation, unless it is proved that accident had taken place due to his negligence.
The claimant and his parents had spent huge amount for his treatment.
His health condition is nothing but a living vegetable and he has been suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 100%.
Therefore, prayed to allow the claim petition and award just and reasonable amount of compensation.
13. The learned advocate for Respondent No.2 has vehemently contended that the alleged offended car was not at all involved in the accident.

Owner, driver and claimant NC: 2023:KHC:41711-DB have colluded and fabricated story of accident in collusion with police, to facilitate claimant to get the compensation from Insurer i.e., Respondent No.2.
Accident was said to be taken place on 22.08.2019 and FIR was registered after lapse of four days i.e., on 26.08.2019.

The reasons assigned in the complaint is that uncle of the claimant was busy in providing treatment to the claimant,
therefore he could not file the complaint in time.
The said reason is not probable, since uncle of the claimant was not his guardian.
Claimant has parents, elder brothers and accident was said to be occurred near his village.
According to the evidence of PW-1, his brother was in the hospital to attend him.
Similarly, his father was taking care of him.

Under those circumstances, reasons assigned in the FIR/complaint that uncle of the complainant was engaged in providing treatment to claimant, therefore he could not file complaint in time, is not a justifiable reason.

In all probability,
the offended car was falsely implicated in the incident; time was taken for deliberation and discussion with owner and driver of the car by the complainant and only after agreement, the complaint NC: 2023:KHC:41711-DB was lodged against the driver of the car for causing accident in question.
14.

Learned advocate for respondent has further submitted that even in the complaint, which was lodged about four days after the alleged accident, in one breath, it is stated that an unknown vehicle dashed against the claimant's motorcycle and in the next breath, it is stated that the said vehicle was Car bearing Registration No.KA-06-ES- 1151.

It creates serious doubt about involvement of the Car.
15.

It is further submitted by learned advocate for respondent No.2 that at the time of filing the complaint, the said Car number was known to the claimant, therefore, there was no question of mentioning it as an unknown Car.
It also indicates that truth came out from the statement of the complainant.

And it is also worth to note that for a period of four days from the accident, both the Sri Shoheb Akthar vs Aleem on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51980514/
4 said vehicle were parked at the place of accident, which is a narrow public road.

sentences.text: Both the vehicles were left at the place of accident un- attended.
It also indicates that the car was falsely - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:41711-DB implicated.
It is not clear as to when the said vehicle was shifted to police station and inspected by the motor vehicle inspector.
All these stories are fabricated only to claim the compensation.

16. It is further submitted by the learned advocate for respondent No.2 that driver of the Car pretending himself as very honest and pleads guilty for causing accident in question and under Section 134 of Motor Vehicles Act, it is his bounden duty to intimate to the nearest police station about the accident or provide the treatment to the injured.
But he has not done both the legal obligation.
It also indicates that accident had not taken place by the said vehicle and it was falsely implicated.
17. The learned counsel for Respondent No.2 has further submitted that alleged car is said to be a Cab/Taxi.
The alleged accident was said to be taken place on 22.08.2019.

It was said to be at the place of incident till drawing of the mahazar, i.e., on 26.08.2019 and thereafter, the said Car was kept in the police station till 06.09.2019 - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:41711-DB and on that day, it was said to be inspected by Motor Vehicle Inspector in the police station and it is not clear whether the owner of the said Car has taken the interim custody of the said vehicle from the Court or not.

On 30.10.2019, police submitted the charge-sheet to the Court and before issue of summons to accused on the very same day, the accused appeared before the Court and pleaded guilty for the alleged offence and paid fine.
All these facts also indicates about the false implication of the offended vehicle in the alleged accident.
The Tribunal has considered these points and rightly dismissed the claim petition.
It does not call for any interference by this Court.

18. The learned advocate for Respondent No.2/ Insurer has further submitted that the motor vehicle compensation case is a benevolent legislation and it is to provide the financial assistance to the victim of an accident or legal heirs of the victim of an accident.
However, the compensation should be paid to a genuine victim of an accident and not otherwise.
The claimant was minor at the time of alleged incident.
The owner of the said motorcycle - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:41711-DB knowingly had given his vehicle to minor, who had no driving license to drive the said kind of vehicle.
Even there is no evidence that claimant was well versed in riding motorcycle.
It appears, he might be riding the vehicle carelessly and in that process, fell down without collecting with any vehicle and sustained injuries.

Only to claim the compensation, the Sri Shoheb Akthar vs Aleem on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51980514/
5 offended car was falsely implicated in collusion with the owner, driver and police.

sentences.text: Under these circumstances, the claim petition has to be dismissed with compensatory costs.
19. We have anxiously gone through the record.
The submission of learned Advocate for Respondent No.2 is acceptable.
The Tribunal has discussed all these facts in the impugned judgment.
The Tribunal has appreciated the pleadings and evidence of the parties and came to conclusion that the said car was falsely implicated in the said accident.

It is settled law that delay in filing complaint or (FIR) registering of a case of accident, may not be fatal to claim compensation in motor vehicle claim petitions or ground for rejection of the claim petition, if there are proper and acceptable explanations for the said delay.

In this case, the - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:41711-DB only explanation offered in the complaint by the complainant, who is said to be uncle of claimant, is that he was busy in providing treatment to claimant, therefore he did not file the complaint in time.

As rightly submitted by learned Advocate for Respondent No.2, the uncle of claimant was not guardian of the claimant and claimant has parents, elder brothers, and according to the evidence of PW.1, his brother as well as father were attending him in the hospital.
Under these circumstances, the reasons assigned by the uncle of complainant for delay in lodging of the complaint after delay of four days certainly creates serious doubt about the accident.
20. The learned advocate for appellant could not respond to the said ground raised by respondent No.2.
The accident had taken place on 22.08.2019.
Complaint was given to the police on 26.08.2019 and thereafter investigation was commenced.
Till then, both the motorcycle as well as the offended Car were said to be at the spot of accident, which is a public road, i.e., Sirivara to Nagavalli Tar Road.
The claimant is said to be resident of Nagavalli village.

It is difficult to believe that none of the residents of the said village informed the police when the two vehicles were laying on the road at the spot of accident un-attended and might be causing inconvenience to the movement of the vehicles on the said road.

In the mahazar, at once it is mentioned that accident had taken place on the Tar Road at the northern end, and in another breath, it is mentioned as accident had taken place on the footpath which is situated beyond the Tar Road and the Investigating Officer even has not seized the glass pieces, broken head light pieces and the broken piece of number plate of the said Car from spot of accident.
They might be important piece of evidence in favour of the prosecution, in the criminal case registered to the accident in question.
The vehicle was seized on 26th August 2019, but it was inspected on 6th September 2019, in the police station compound.
It appears, the owner of the said vehicle did not bother about the said vehicle.
It was said to be not in his custody from 22nd August 2019 till he took possession of the property.

About four days, it was laying on the main road going from Sirivara to Nagavalli and thereafter, in the police - 15 - Sri Shoheb Akthar vs Aleem on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51980514/
6 NC: 2023:KHC:41711-DB station compound, which is also very much doubtful, which is noted by the Tribunal.
21.
The claimant has not examined his uncle, who lodged the complaint, for explaining the reason for delay in filing the complaint.
Moreover, PW-1 did not explain the delay in filing the complaint in his evidence.
Under these circumstances, the submission of learned Advocate for Respondent No.2 about false implication of the offended Car in the said accident cannot be ruled out.
22. The Tribunal has discussed in detail about the said evidence and came to conclusion that the vehicle was falsely implicated in this case.
Therefore, the Respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify the owner of the vehicle or pay the compensation.
And on that ground, the Tribunal has dismissed the claim petition.
We do not find any illegality or irregularity in the said findings.

23. We have every sympathy to the claimant, but that cannot be a ground to award compensation,
when the claimant failed to prove the accident in question and - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:41711-DB evidence, facts and circumstances indicates false implication of the car in the alleged incident and claimant is unable to prove that by involvement of the said vehicle, accident had taken place.
Admittedly, the claimant was minor and he had no driving license to ride the motorcycle at the time of alleged accident and he was given motorcycle by the owner of the said vehicle.

The submission of learned advocate for respondent No.2 that claimant himself might have fell down because of his own negligence or he might have met with an accident due to his own negligence and to claim the compensation from the Insurance Companies, implicated the car in collusion with owner and driver of the car and police cannot be ruled out.

In such event, the Court cannot blindly award the compensation, only on the ground that the victim has been suffering from permanent disability and he had spent huge amount towards medical and incidental expenses.
24. It is pertinent to note that had claimant proved the accident by involvement of said car, then only he would be entitled for compensation.

However, in this case,
- 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:41711-DB the claimant has utterly failed to establish and prove that the said vehicle was involved in the accident and the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the said vehicle, by its driver.
The Tribunal had discussed pleading and evidence in detail and held that claimant had failed to prove the accident by involvement of offended vehicle.
The said findings do not call for interference by this Court.
25. In view of the above said reasons, we concur with the findings of the Tribunal.

Accordingly, we pass the following:
ORDER
